record.original_question: For the DNA alignment example whose model M is the set of positive 4×4 matrices (pij) of rank at most 2 and whose likelihood function is L = (∏i pii)^4 · (∏i≠j pij)^2 · (∑i,j pij)^−40, is the matrix (1/40)·[[3,3,2,2],[3,3,2,2],[2,2,3,3],[2,2,3,3]] a global maximum of L?

evidence.quote: Here the model M consists of all (positive) 4×4-matrices (pij ) of rank at most two. In the given alignment, each match occurs four times and each mismatch occurs two times. Hence the likelihood function (3.1) equals L = (∏i pii)^4 · (∏i≠j pij)^2 · (∑i,j pij)^−40.
Based on experiments with the EM algorithm, we conjectured that the matrix (pˆij) = 1/40 [[3, 3, 2, 2], [3, 3, 2, 2], [2, 2, 3, 3], [2, 2, 3, 3]] is a global maximum of the likelihood function L.
I offered a cash prize of 100 Swiss Francs for the resolution of this very specific conjecture, and this prize remains unclaimed and is still available at this time (August 2007).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be the set of positive real $4\times 4$ matrices $P=(p_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le 4}$ of rank at most $2$, with all entries strictly positive. Define the likelihood function
$$L(P) \;=\; \Bigl(\prod_{i=1}^{4} p_{ii}\Bigr)^{4} \cdot \Bigl(\prod_{i\ne j} p_{ij}\Bigr)^{2} \cdot \Bigl(\sum_{i,j} p_{ij}\Bigr)^{-40}.$$
Determine whether the matrix
$$\hat P \;=\; \frac{1}{40}\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 3 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & 3 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$$
is a global maximum of $L$ on $M$.
artifact.category_tag: Algebraic statistics / maximum likelihood on rank-constrained matrices
artifact.status_search_result: The "100 Swiss Francs problem" of Sturmfels was resolved in 2008 by Mingfu Zhu (and elaborated in subsequent work, e.g., Gross–Drton–Sullivant and Hauenstein–Rodriguez–Sturmfels), confirming that the proposed matrix is indeed a global maximum of the likelihood function. The published account "Solving the 100 Swiss Francs Problem" (Math. in Computer Science, 2011) presents the solution.

status_evidence.title: Solving the 100 Swiss Francs Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Sturmfels offered 100 Swiss Francs ... for the solution of a particular 4×4 instance ... that prize was won by Mingfu Zhu
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture was solved, confirming the proposed matrix is a global maximum.

status_evidence.title: Maximum Likelihood for Matrices with Rank Constraints
status_evidence.snippet: the third author offered a cash prize of 100 Swiss Francs ... That prize was won in 2008 by Mingfu Zhu
status_evidence.claim: The 100 Swiss Francs conjecture was resolved in 2008.
